The inspection was related to a reported brine release from valve on a brine tank by the operator. The operator reported a spill of approximately 22 BBLs of brine from a brine water transfer line on 2/25/19. The operator reported that a valve at the brine storage tank in an earthen dike has broken releasing the brine into the earthen dike. The operator has reported that the brine was captured and stored in the earthen dike around the tanks. At time of inspection standing brine was noted in the dike and the soil conductivity readings in the dike were Over Readings (Or) or greater than 20 mS. Oil stained/saturated soil was noted near the well head and production equipment.

Comments: On February 19, 2025, the Department conducted a Routine Partial Inspection of Apollo Energy's Dewitt 1 well, located in Georges Township, Fayette County.At the time of this inspection, the access road to the well site had 2-4 inch deep ruts that were filled in with frozen stormwater and mud that stretched the entire length of the access road, and the access road did not appear to be stabilized with vegetation or gravel. The Department recommends the Operator conduct maintenance on the access road to stabilize it. The vegetative cover of the well site could not be assessed at this time due to snow cover. properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Twp, Bradford County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/12/2022 to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/12/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 978343
Permit API: 015-23678
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2022
Comments: Site inspection conducted as a follow up to Notice of Violations (NOV) associated inspection report #3373528 dated 6/6/2022 and administrative inspection report #3386649 dated 7/5/2022. There are no Blackhill Energy personnel on site at time of inspection. Weather conditions are overcast and 31 degrees F. During this inspection, completions equipment is still attached to the wells drilled and stimulated during 2021. Two sand separators and a 500 barrel gas buster tank appear to be connected to gas wells (photo 2). Puddled fluid on site was screened using an Oakton PCTS 50 water conductivity meter and a Hanna Groline soil conductivity meter. While screening puddles around the well heads and 500 barrel gas buster frac tank, the Department observed fluid draining from the tank and releasing onto secondary containment (photo 3). The containment is open along the north end discharge port and puddled fluid on containment appears to be flowing off containment into the pad surface (photo 4). Water within containment is observed with conductivity reading 'Over Range' (>19.99 mS/cm). Puddles screened outside of containment are observed to range between 9.8 mS/cm near the north well head to 'Over Range' in a puddle next to the tank secondary containment. Sample 4406-018 collected at 11:45 from fluid puddled on pad rock surface between tank secondary containment and north-most gas well (photo 7). Sample will be analyzed using SAC 942. The Department notified Regina Logue, Blackhill Energy Environmental Manager, that the tank was leaking at 12:15. Ms. Logue indicated that Blackhill personnel were en route to the site and that Moody's Environmental was contracted to conduct site characterization. Violation noted for potential pollution. Additional violations may be issued pending results of water sample analysis. Previous NOV's associated with inspection report #3373528 dated 6/6/2022 and administrative inspection report #3386649 dated 7/5/2022 remain outstanding.

Comments: On November 8, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection for a reported spill at the Inflection Energy TLC Pad. The DEP received a phone call from Inflection Energy Zac Subra on November 6, 2021 about a release of production fluid during a pressure test. The DEP met with Inflection Energy Joe Zoka. During a pressure test for the preparation of flowback of the recently drilled wells, a valve was left open. The open valve spilled about 28 gallons of brine fluid to the pad surface. The impacted area was excavated immediately. Inflection scraped about 3 inches of a 15 ft. by 10 ft. area. The impacted soil was then loaded into a covered container to be hauled to the landfill. The containment around the flowback equipment appears to be in good condition. Inflection is planning to begin flowback process on Tuesday. Violations of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), ¿78a.56(a), and SWMA 301 are noted but have been immediately corrected. Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Report 3257683.

Comments: On July 27 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3491397,3387914, 3514511 and 3543627. Accompanying into today's inspection was the landowner. The findings were as follows: According to the Order issued to the operator by the Department for this site, the Operator shall completely restore the well site within 9 months after plugging. The well site and access road are not restored during today's inspection, not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. According to the landowner, the site has not been restored to pre-existing contours.The well was plugged on October 7, 2021 according the the plugging certificate submitted by the Operator for this well. As such, the Operator was to completely restore the well site no later than July 7, 2022. E and S Plan has not been received by the Department as previously requested in IRs 3262679, 3387914, 3514511 and 3543627. No E and S Plan was found on site. Lack of adequate uniform vegetation is still observed due to multiple areas of exposed soil and rock. There are several bare spots throughout the former well site that are lacking adequate uniform vegetation. No E and S BMPs are installed on site. The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. The Department recommends the Operator take necessary measures to ensure 70% uniform vegetative growth is achieved for restoration of the site. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.The transmission of this inspection is delayed due to an IT error.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Repsol Oil & Gas Usa Llc

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 848033
Permit API: 015-23420
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Columbia Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-04-25
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's Monro G (03-142) Well Pad in Columbia Twp, Bradford County on 4/25/2019 at 0830 hours. The weather was sunny and 50 degrees. The inspection was conducted in response to a notice to the department that on 4/25/2019, during the 2nd stage of the 3H well, a piece of iron washed out and released a mixture of frack fluid and sand to containment. The washout created a "jetstream" of fluid with a reported ~9000 PSI of pressure behind it. This stream of fluid cut through the secondary containment liner, the primary containment liner, and dug through some pad material. An estimated 15 gallons of frack fluid and sand mixture was released through the hole. A vac truck was onsite to recover sand/fluid mixture from containment. Most of the fluid was recovered. The vac truck was also used to suck fluid that had collected in the hole through containment. While I was onsite, crew was flowing back and flushing the well to be able to shut it down. After shutting the well down, we were able to assess the impacted area. Golder was onsite screening the area off the northern edge of the pad. No evidence of impact was reported and I didn't observe any impacts off containment besides the hole that was created. The area of the containment that was breached was just east of the 5H wellhead. The hole was approximately 1 foot wide. Golder screened the soil as far into the void as possible. Their highest recorded reading from the impacted soil was 2.53ms/cm. No standing liquid was visible downhole. Small amounts of fluid remained on the containment and I obtained a reading of 17-18ms/cm from one of them (see photo #6). Kris Perritt agreed that this fluid would be representable to the fluid out of containment. Kris plans to have the iron, rig mats, and containment pulled back to learn the extent of the void to fill it in for safety purposes. Upon soil screening of the area, impacted soils would be excavated and disposed of. Golder planned on taking soil samples from beneath the containment and the sampling results would be forwarded to the DEP. Due to findings throughout the course of this inspection, violations of the following are cited against well API #015-23420: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 35 P.S. 6018.301

Comments: On site today in response to a water complaint in the area. This is a FUI (Follow Up Inspection) for the (4) wells on the pad that were inspected on 10/14/21. Remedial work was completed on the 2H, 4H and 6H wells at the end of 2017 to address previous violations cited on the 6H well. - Met w/ lease operator Ben Whitaker to perform isolated gas screenings of the cemented annuli. - All (4) wells have the (20x13) and (13x9) annuli isolated and venting to atmosphere. Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8265579
Permit API: 015-21874
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Overton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/24/2026
Comments: Incident Inspection of Expand's "Oil Can" Marcellus well site.Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP on Monday (Preisdents Day) February 16, 2026 to report an estimated 30 gallon release of produced liquid (brine) from a tank battery. Moyer explained that a vac truck was filling a 500 barrel tank with brine and it overflowed into secondary liner containment. Approximately 3 gallons of the brine splashed onto the pad surface, and a liner breach leaked some of the brine onto the pad surface. The brine is stored on this pad for hydraulically fracturing Marcellus wells at other Expand sites. Expand removed 4 of the 500 barrel tanks February 18-19 to expose the impacted pad surface for excavation.I spoke with Dakota Manning (Crescent Environmental) on site. He explained they are removing liquid from snow melt that is flowing into the excavated area. They plan to obtain soil samples to comply with Act 2 after the melt liquid stops flowing into the sump. Crescent got electrical conductivity readings of 0.6-1.0 mS/cm from the liquid in the sump.Violations for the brine release are cited to the 015-21874 permit.Cannot assess soil stabilization because ~6 of snow cover. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.There is snow in all 3 Marcellus cellars.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed.Pooled liquid on the pad surface has electrical conductivity of 0.15-0.33 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.Air temp 24FJLP

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/03/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/03/2026
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8284091
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

Comments: On July 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4209208, where violations were continued for broken and corroded piping causing a release, as well as the issuance of new violations for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.Accompanying on today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4209208, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it, however the well tag does not appear to updated and the phone number listed on the tag is not in service. Violations are being continued at this time for having inaccurate information on the well tag/posting. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank ((3.80 mS and Over Range (>12mS)) and adjacent to the broken corroded pipe (0.329 mS). These conductivity readings were compared to a background soil conductivity reading of 0.181 mS collected upslope and away from the release area. The soil conductivity readings in the release area are elevated compared to background subjugating that the release from the back of the production tank on the right has yet to be remediated. Violations are being continued at this time for the release from the production tank.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment. Violations are being continued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. The Department is again requesting the Operator provide the Department with a Notice of Violation Operator response within 14 days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping, inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site is to remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: On 5/06/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection in response to a complaint (CTS-397312) at the Clara Jacques 1 well plugging site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. This inspection also follows-up to IR 4186065, where violations were issued against severe tire rutting observed in the access road.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site after in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216; after completion of plugging operations.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance along Five Forks Road (photos 1 and 2). An additional RCE is installed where the access road meets the well site, in accordance with the E and S plan drawing. The RCE adjacent to the well plugging site is laden with sediment (photos 15 and 22). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed on site in the locations shown on E and S plan drawing (photos 9, 12, 17, 19, and 20). Significant tire rutting remains throughout the access road. Due to the soft and damp soil conditions that appear to exist on site, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator consider additional E and S control measures as necessary, to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring on site. Well plugging equipment was observed on site, however plugging operations do not appear to be occurring at the time of inspection. A puddle with swirly rainbow sheen was observed adjacent to well plugging rig. This swirly rainbow sheen remained intact when disturbed, which is a known indicator of a petroleum-based release.The Department identified an access road cross-culvert at the time of IR 4186065 (photo 23). No loose sediment was observed in the cross-culvert during this inspection. However, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator take necessary measures to ensure that the cross-culvert is protected from sedimentation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4186065 shall remain outstanding. Additional violations shall be issued for failure to adequately protect the cross-culvert shown in Photo 14 and for failure maintain the RCE adjacent to the well plugging site. Additional volations may be forthcoming against the swirly rainbow sheen released adjacent to the well plugging rig.

Comments: On 05/14/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Cogar Well Site following an incident report received by the Department on 05/12/2025 (CTS 389093). SPSI crew on site remediating. The operator reported a spill to the Department on 05/13/2025 regarding more than 5 gallons of production water that were released on a load out pumpkin. No waterways were affected. The incident occurred on 05/12/2025 and reported over two hours after the incident on 05/13/2025. The following was observed:The area of impact was adjacent to the containment of the production tanks. SPSI excavated the impacted area to determine the extent of impact and place waste in roll off dumpsters. The area of impact was under the load out pumpkin and where the cement containment would be. A portion of the dump line was exposed during excavation. Water was pooling within the excavated area (Photos 1-6).Conductivity readings were taken within the area of impact. Readings were 5.23, 7.60, 13.62, 14.27, 16.22 mS/cm, and Over Range (Photos 7-14).Additional readings taken within the upper layers of substrate and clay layer were 430, 533, 850, and 968 uS/cm (Photos 15-18).The cement containment had a reading of Over Range. There appeared to be residual fluid combined with rainwater (Photo 19).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan were on site (Photo 20).Due to the release of production fluid greater than 5 gallons and failure to report a reportable spill within 2 hours, violations of 78a54, SWMA 301, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), 78a66(b)2 are being issued. The Department requests an updated estimation of the quantity of production fluid released. The Department requests information on if the operator intends to remediate per Act 2 guidelines regarding the quantity released.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/24/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8226507
Permit API: 015-23923
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/24/2025
Comments: On 03/21/2025 the DEP received a spill/release on the pad surface notification (CTS #387689) from representative Steve Moyer. Steve stated "they noticed a stain about 45' x 25' next to the wellheads off containment on gravel. The conductivity was high. Estimating about 1 to 1.5 barrels of produced water was released. An environmental consultant was contacted who will scrape up material." On 03/24/2025 at 0750 hours the DEP spoke with representative Steve Moyer. He stated that there was a leak within the secondary containment that led to this release. A crew scraped the material on 03/21/2025. New gravel has be placed in the 45' x 25' reported release area (photo #2). Upon further investigation it was determined that a crew had been onsite pumping brine down a well to stop the flow to be able to change the wellhead master valve. After they completed work and the area began to dry out a crystal staining was observed. On 03/24/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection for Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) STETHERS Location Well Pad in Wyalusing Township, Bradford County. The weather was 42 degrees and cloudy. I arrived at 0940 hours. A representative onsite stated the recovered material from the 03/21/2025 release was removed from the site the same day. Recovered material from the 01/29/2025 discovered release (Inspection Report #3907635 and 3919693) was also being removed from the site on 03/21/2025 and continued to be removed during the incident response inspection report on 03/24/2025 (photo #10).Due to the quantity of the release this is being referred to ECB for Act 2 compliance. Violations against API #015-23923 (Inspection Report #3907635 and 3919693, Enforcement ID 437898) remain open:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)Based on the reported release (CTS #387689) additional violations have been cited against API #015-23923: CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 1115 hours.
